correctness.rationale: Prime-square exclusion follows from gcd(p,p²+p+1)=1 and p²+p+1>p−1. For p<q, p=2 forces q+1|4, hence q=3. For odd p,q, set m=(q+1)/2|p(p−1). If p∤m then m=p−1 and integrality forces p+1|15, impossible as even≥4. If p|m, put m=pa and p−1=ab: exact rearrangement gives ab+2 | b−4a−6. The positive and zero cases fail (zero gives composite q), and with 4a+6−b=t(ab+2), cases t≥3,1 give even p or composite q; t=2 forces b=2 and q=p²−p−1. Substituting that prime q gives integer ratio q(p−2). Independently generated prime factorizations and checked 210035 Ω=2 integers up to 10^6; exactly 13 hits 6,15,95,287,1199,4607,23519,28799,101567,223199,296207,352799,903167 obey the formula. Infinite proof does not depend on finite sieve.
